objective: Five copies of one text normaliser become one. Four test modules carried a private _norm and tests/showcase_parity.py already exported the same function, more completely. #341 asked for the copies to be merged and for the one real question - whether a tag becomes nothing or a space - to be decided explicitly rather than inherited.
completed: tests/showcase_parity.py gains norm_markup(), the strict sibling of norm(): markup and backticks out, Markdown emphasis and links left alone.
Four modules import it instead of defining _norm; five definitions of the shared behaviour become two named functions with different jobs.
The tag question is settled by experiment and recorded in norm()'s docstring, where the choice is made.
Review's eight record-side divergences are caught again - two per module, each of which passed under the first attempt.
All four modules' declared page-side controls still fire, and each module's docstring now records the WP-110 re-run rather than leaving the evidence in a commit message.
Three dead `import html as html_mod` lines removed from modules that no longer normalise for themselves.
The dual-import idiom is used, so the modules run by discovery and by module name from the root; both exercised.
remaining: Two-axis review of the head commit, then merge.

validation.command: wp110_exact_inputs.py - old vs new on every fragment the four modules actually normalise

observations: The first attempt WEAKENED all four guards and the suite did not notice. Review constructed eight record-side divergences - a cell gaining `**bold**`, a cell becoming `[text](url)` where the page says something else - and every one was caught at the base commit and passed after the refactor. norm() resolves Markdown links and strips bold, so a link's target became invisible to the comparison entirely. The justification for adopting it, that those steps were 'improvements on the record side', was asserted and never checked: no cell in any region those four compare contains a link or a bold marker.

That is the exact failure #341's fourth criterion warned about, and my own controls missed it. The four I re-ran were each module's own declared controls, but all four are page-side plain-text edits that any normaliser catches; none exercised the behaviour that had changed. A control has to exercise the change, not merely exist.

Making norm() stricter for everyone was tried before adding a sibling, and the suite refused it: dropping the link step fails test_epics_match_the_plan and norm()'s own self-tests, because the records those readers compare do carry Markdown emphasis and links. So the leniency is real and needed - by other callers - and the two behaviours are two named functions rather than one with a boolean.

The tag question was decided by experiment rather than preference. Making the module that spaced tags drop them leaves the suite green; making the other three space them fails test_work_package_loop_page, whose page writes a citation as '(Discover 03)' against a record writing '(Discover 03)'. Its docstring had predicted exactly that case, so the experiment confirmed a comment nobody had tested.

One claim of mine was corrected rather than defended: I said test_phase_pages.py would 'change behaviour to no purpose' if it adopted the shared function. Review adopted it there and the suite stayed green. Excluding it is still right - it would inherit the leniency - but the stated reason was asserted, not demonstrated.

The correction is proved behaviour-preserving rather than asserted to be. Each module's own reader was run with _norm captured, and old and new compared on exactly the arguments it passes: 96 fragments for the operations page, 19 for the hub, 18 for the team model, 144 for the Work Package loop - 277 in all, ZERO differences, including the module whose implementation changed from spacing tags to dropping them. A broader corpus of whole contents showed 42 apparent differences for that module, all of the shape 'E1Tenant Scale', and all of them artefacts of the corpus builder: that module's own regex splits the identifier cell before _norm ever sees it. Checking what a function is actually called with beats checking what it could be called with.
decisions: DEC-112: four copies adopt showcase_parity.norm; a tag becomes nothing, settled by experiment.
assumptions: showcase_parity.norm doing strictly more than the copies it replaces - Markdown links resolved, bold markers stripped - is safe because both sides of every comparison pass through it, and the suite confirms it.

stop_if: A module's private normaliser is replaced without re-running that module's own declared negative control.
test_showcase_pages.py or test_phase_pages.py is made to adopt the shared function; theirs are different by design.

declared_non_coverage: Only _norm is consolidated. designs() keeps its four variants, which differ deliberately - one excludes the security proof, one is keyed by epic - and unifying them needs parameters, as WP-109 measured.
The controls re-run here are the ones each module declares; a defect a module never claimed to catch is still not caught.

The four modules are now STRICTER than before only in the sense that they are no longer looser; norm_markup reproduces exactly the behaviour their private copies had, except that one of them stops spacing tags.
Only 4 of the 17 controls those modules declare were re-run, plus review's 8. The other 13 are unchanged and were not exercised.
